record.original_question: Fix an integer d >= 2. For each n, let p_{n,d}(t) = Product_{i=1}^n (1 + t^i + ... + t^{i(d-1)}), equivalently the generating function for partitions of integers at most (d-1)n(n+1)/2 having at most n parts with each part repeated at most d-1 times. Are the coefficients of p_{n,d}(t) unimodal for all sufficiently large n?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.4 (Almkvist ’85). For every fixed d ≥ 2, the polynomial pn,d(t) has unimodal coefficients for n sufficiently large.

Let pn,d(t) be the generating function for the number of partitions of integers smaller than or equal to (d−1)n(n+ 1)/2 with at most n parts and each part repeated at most d − 1 times. It is known that pn,d(t) = Π^n_{i=1}(1 + t^i + · · · + t^{i(d−1)}).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For integers $d\ge 2$ and $n\ge 1$, define the polynomial
$$p_{n,d}(t) \;=\; \prod_{i=1}^{n}\bigl(1+t^{i}+t^{2i}+\cdots+t^{i(d-1)}\bigr)\in\mathbb{Z}[t].$$
Equivalently, $p_{n,d}(t)=\sum_{k\ge 0} a_{n,d}(k)\,t^{k}$ where $a_{n,d}(k)$ is the number of partitions of $k$ into at most $n$ parts, each part repeated at most $d-1$ times (so $0\le k\le (d-1)n(n+1)/2$). A polynomial $\sum_{k} c_k t^k$ with real coefficients is called unimodal if there exists an index $k^{*}$ such that $c_0\le c_1\le\cdots\le c_{k^{*}}\ge c_{k^{*}+1}\ge\cdots$.

Question: Fix an integer $d\ge 2$. Is it true that for all sufficiently large $n$, the coefficient sequence of $p_{n,d}(t)$ is unimodal?
artifact.status_search_result: Almkvist's 1985 conjecture is widely cited as still open in general. Partial results exist (e.g., for small $d$ or under additional hypotheses; recent works in 2024–2025 establish Lefschetz-type strengthenings in special two-parameter cases), but no proof of the full conjecture for all $d\ge 2$ and large $n$ is known.

status_evidence.title: Lattice Paths, Lefschetz Properties, and Almkvist's Conjecture in Two Variables
status_evidence.snippet: We address a strengthening of a conjecture of Almkvist on the unimodality of certain Hilbert functions...
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2024) work treats a strengthened form of Almkvist's conjecture in special cases, indicating the general conjecture is still studied as open.

status_evidence.title: Unimodality via Kronecker products (Pak–Panova)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Almkvist's conjecture and partial progress on unimodality of products of q-integers.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys note Almkvist's conjecture remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: Unimodality of Certain Partition Polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Proves unimodality of related partition polynomials in specific families.
status_evidence.claim: Continuing partial progress; full Almkvist conjecture not resolved.
